3a615dd113.q: What is the difference between developing a clinical niche and becoming too narrowly focused as a dietitian?
3a615dd113.a: Having a niche does not mean you only do one thing. You retain all your previous experience and skills, and can always pull from those other areas if needed. The basic science and human body principles are transferable across specialties, so you are honing in on certain areas versus others while keeping the broader knowledge foundation intact.
3a615dd113.e: Finding Your Expertise and Owning It
3a615dd113.rq: Expertise is the continuum. It is all about your willingness to be curious, to learn and to grow.

79abcaff95.q: How can registered dietitians identify whether they should pursue a specialty credential like CNSC?
79abcaff95.a: Consider the exam fees and cost of materials which are not inexpensive and require every five-year renewal. Choose something you are genuinely interested in to make studying easier. Think about how it will benefit you, such as highlighting your skill set on a resume in a competitive job market, opening up opportunities for more pay, different positions, or professional connections.

ee0356210c.q: How can dietitians with expertise demonstrate their knowledge without promoting themselves?
ee0356210c.a: It is less about promoting yourself and more about using your personality, strengths, and gifts to advocate for the patient. Being confident in your knowledge, consistently showing up, speaking up, and communicating kindly and professionally with your team demonstrates that you are a valuable resource and builds trust.

128b66fc3a.q: What is expertise according to Laura Oltman's perspective after 20 years in dietetics?
128b66fc3a.a: Expertise is a continuum, not a fixed destination. It is all about willingness to be curious, to learn and to grow. Growth comes through challenges like complex patients or seeking out opportunities, and even the most respected dietitians are always learning because nutrition is constantly growing and changing.
